answer: Each epoch, agents must answer a challenge word drawn from a randomness beacon, weaving it into a signed proof-of-liveness message tied to their staked identity. Because words like lantern, umber, or copper appear only after the beacon commits, a sybil attacker cannot precompute template answers; each fake identity needs live key material, a fresh signature, and its own stake, so mass-creating personas costs real capital plus per-epoch computation, and any identity that misses or reuses a stale answer is slashed and pruned automatically.
